blocks.text: The argument culminates in the rejection of older markers, shrine cults, and submissive habits, and then turns into a new sakhi of origin at Kesgarh about the birth of the Khalsa Panth. (36; Episode 15, 1)

At Kesgarh Sahib the Guru consults learned men, fixes the undertaking, and selects five youths drawn across caste lines, making visible a new brotherhood rather than a continuation of older hierarchy. (2–5)
These first Panj Pyare are gathered for the preparation of amrit, with water, sweetness, and the double-edged sword brought together under the Guru’s direction to begin the new initiation. (5–6)
